events.title: Great Lisbon Earthquake
events.description: On All Saints' Day, a massive earthquake estimated at magnitude 8.5-9.0 struck Lisbon, Portugal, followed by a tsunami and fires that destroyed much of the city and killed tens of thousands of people.
events.significance: One of the deadliest earthquakes in history, it profoundly influenced Enlightenment thought, prompting debate among philosophers such as Voltaire and Rousseau about divine providence, and it helped lay the groundwork for modern seismology.

events.title: Sistine Chapel Ceiling Unveiled
events.description: Michelangelo's frescoes on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel in Vatican City were publicly unveiled by Pope Julius II after about four years of work.
events.significance: The ceiling, including The Creation of Adam, is regarded as a supreme achievement of High Renaissance art and has influenced Western art for centuries.

events.title: Attempted Assassination of President Harry S. Truman
events.description: Two Puerto Rican nationalists, Oscar Collazo and Griselio Torresola, attempted to assassinate President Truman at Blair House in Washington, D.C. Torresola and White House police officer Leslie Coffelt were killed in the gunfight.
events.significance: The attack was one of the few attempts on a sitting U.S. president's life and brought attention to the Puerto Rican independence movement while prompting tighter presidential security.

events.title: United States Detonates First Hydrogen Bomb
events.description: The United States tested 'Ivy Mike' at Enewetak Atoll in the Pacific, the first successful full-scale thermonuclear device, with a yield of about 10.4 megatons.
events.significance: The test escalated the Cold War nuclear arms race, as the hydrogen bomb was hundreds of times more powerful than the atomic bombs used in 1945.

events.title: Maastricht Treaty Takes Effect
events.description: The Treaty on European Union came into force, formally establishing the European Union and laying the groundwork for a single currency and common foreign and security policy.
events.significance: It transformed the European Community into the European Union, deepening political and economic integration across Europe and paving the way for the euro.
